input.rationale: Trace how a restarted node re-establishes its configuration ('context validity') when the committed-log replay feature is enabled. NewRaft replays committed logs first (restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index) and then scans the log for configuration entries starting at max(lastSnapshot, lastApplied)+1. Because the scan is skipped over the committed prefix, configuration entries inside it are never applied to r.configurations when no snapshot carries them, even though they remain in the log. Focused probe: restart a single-voter node that was bootstrapped and applied commands but never snapshotted, with RestoreCommittedLogs on/off and with a covering snapshot as control. Reproducibility question: the dual-majority outcome depends on the ordering between the partitioned side's election and the stale leader's lease, so its successor experiment is repeated once from its retained inputs in a clean copy to see whether the concurrent-leader window and the truncation of the committed entry recur under schedule variation. Reproducibility question: the corrected resurrected-voter experiment is repeated once from its retained inputs in a clean copy, because the premature-commit observation depends on the stale leader winning its re-election after the restart and on the removed voter having caught up before the partition. Reproducibility question: the forgotten-added-voter experiment is repeated once from its retained inputs in a clean copy, since the premature commit depends on the restarted leader winning its re-election with an understated quorum and on the partition leaving exactly two connected voters. Reproducibility question: the three-voter simultaneous-restart experiment is repeated once from its retained inputs in a clean copy, because the progress claim (no leader while every voter holds the configuration only in its log) is the headline liveness consequence and currently rests on a single scored execution with its control. Reproducibility question: the original restart probe (whose receipt is the most cited witness of the empty-configuration case, including its own non-replay and snapshot controls in one execution) is repeated once from its retained inputs in a clean copy, to confirm that the primary witness and both in-harness controls reproduce together. Reproducibility question: the partial-restart experiment is repeated once from its retained inputs in a clean copy, because that harness contains the timing-dependent half of the progress claim (which node leads after two of three voters restart) as well as the structural half (a live quorum that cannot elect once the configured voter stops). Correction of the repeat target: the repeat just executed (receipt 8f0b76d0cd49441c81ecb603f1fcd527) ran the superseded revision of the partial-restart experiment (experiment a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-experiment), whose captured harness still used helpers declared in a sibling file and therefore failed to build before any test ran. The corrected, self-contained revision of that same harness is experiment b826595f01b844f9b95efe7b29d757dd-experiment (retained receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837); the repeat is re-requested against that revision. Reproducibility question: the revision carrying the client-contract observation is repeated once from its retained inputs, because that observation requires the stale leader to still consider itself leader when the confirmation is issued and when the old majority elects, which is schedule-sensitive (one earlier revision saw the leader step down first).

investigations.question: Does a node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, whose newest configuration entry is inside the persisted commit index and has no covering snapshot, still know that configuration after NewRaft returns?
investigations.hypothesis: No. restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so the configuration scan starts after the committed prefix and never calls processConfigurationLogEntry for the configuration entry that only exists in the log. r.configurations.latest stays empty (or stays at the snapshot configuration), so the node loses its own membership context, cannot start elections, and skips the membership checks when granting votes.
investigations.discriminator: Restart the same durable state twice: with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and with RestoreCommittedLogs=false. Predict servers_after=0 and no re-election with the feature on, versus servers_after=1 and a successful re-election with it off. A third run takes a snapshot before restart to show that a snapshot-carried configuration masks the loss (servers_after=1), separating the scanning bound from generic restart damage.

investigations.question: When RestoreCommittedLogs makes a restarted leader forget a committed removal, does the resurrected voter let that leader commit and report success for entries that the configuration committed in the log requires another member (B) to accept?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: A's in-memory configuration still contains the removed voter C, so A's commitment quorum is computed over {A,B,C} and an entry acknowledged by A and C counts as committed even though the configuration committed in the log is {A,B}; A applies it and the client is told it succeeded although B, a member required for any quorum of the committed configuration, never received the entry.
investigations.discriminator: Same cluster and stores with the flag on and off: shut down C, remove it, commit further entries, restart the leader, bring C back so it catches up, partition B, then apply one entry on the leader. Prediction with the flag: the Apply returns success, the leader's commit and applied indexes advance to the new entry, and the entry is absent from B (and from every quorum of {A,B}). Prediction without the flag: the leader's configuration is {A,B}, so the same partition makes the same Apply fail.

investigations.question: When RestoreCommittedLogs makes a restarted leader forget a voter whose addition is committed in its own log, does the resulting smaller in-memory quorum let it accept and apply entries that only a minority of the committed voters hold?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: with the added voter D absent from the restarted leader's configuration, its quorum is two of {A,B,C} instead of three of {A,B,C,D}, so a partition that leaves only A and B connected still lets it commit and apply an entry, and the client is told the write succeeded although a quorum of the committed configuration never received it.
investigations.discriminator: Four voters {A,B,C}+D added after a snapshot, further commits, then restart the leader with the flag on and off; partition C and D from A and apply one entry. Prediction with the flag: the Apply succeeds and only A and B hold the entry; prediction without the flag: the same partition makes the Apply fail.

knowledge.statement: A stale in-memory configuration drives every membership decision of the node: configurationChangeChIfStable admits a configuration change once the stale latest and committed indexes look equal, appendConfigurationEntry derives the next membership from the stale base, commitment is installed from that new configuration on append, and the election quorum, checkLeaderLease and the leadership-confirmation quorum (verifyLeader) all use the latest in-memory configuration. After a restart with RestoreCommittedLogs a node can therefore drop a voter that is only in its log, resurrect a voter whose removal is committed, and count a quorum of the stale membership: it commits and applies entries that a member required by the committed configuration has not accepted, it confirms leadership for clients from that stale quorum while a different majority elects a leader in a higher term, and with a partitioned old voter it can truncate an entry it had committed.
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore and a log whose newest configuration entry lies inside the replayed committed prefix without a covering snapshot; the affected node must lead (or be elected) for the commitment, lease, confirmation and configuration-change consequences.
knowledge.changed_premise: Statement extended, not corrected: the previous revision listed commitment, lease and configuration-change decisions as the consumers of the stale configuration; this revision adds the leadership-confirmation quorum (verifyLeader) and the client-visible consequence observed since (confirmation succeeding while a different majority elects a higher-term leader). Conditions, sources for the original claims and all earlier evidence are unchanged.

gaps.question: Can the silently-created two-server change ({A,B,C} -> {A,B,E}, committed with A plus a promoted caught-up nonvoter E while B is partitioned) let the old majority {B,C} elect a leader in a higher term that then truncates A's committed entry X when the partition heals, and can the two sides therefore hold leaders of different terms over the same log?

interpretations.rationale: Three independent receipts, all retained. (1) 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc index 1: with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot the restarting node returns with an empty configuration (servers_after=0 against servers_before=1), never campaigns again in a 3s opportunity, and logs 'no known peers, aborting election'; both the non-replay run (index 3) and the snapshot run (index 5) keep the configuration and re-elect. (2) d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740 index 1: with a snapshot carrying {A,B}@1 and a committed AddVoter C at index 8 with staged commit 11, the restarted node reports 2 servers while its continuously running peer reports 3 and its own log still holds the newest configuration entry; index 3: a later AddVoter E then returns no error and both nodes converge on 3 members without C (contains_c_final=false), i.e. a legitimately added voter is silently removed from the cluster by a change computed from the stale base. (3) edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d index 1: the isolated control with RestoreCommittedLogs=false scores holds (servers_after=1 against the same bootstrapped voter), so the replayed committed prefix, not restart itself, is the cause. (4) 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a index 1: restarting all three voters at once with the flag leaves servers_after=[0,0,0] and nodes_with_full_config=0 with no leader in a six-second opportunity, while the same procedure without the flag scores holds at index 3 (nodes_with_full_config=3, leader elected) - a cluster-wide progress loss, not a single node's lost context. (5) 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837: with only two of three voters restarted, the untouched configured voter leads with the configuration-less nodes' votes (index 0, servers_after=[0,0,3]); once that voter stops, the two remaining live, fully up-to-date voters cannot elect a leader in six seconds at 50ms timeouts (index 1, log last index 13 on both), while the control without the flag re-elects immediately (index 3). Source chain: restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755); the configuration scan then begins at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never fed to their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). With Servers empty the follower refuses to campaign (raft.go 230-234 on every heartbeat timeout, raft.go 214-251) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784); with Servers stale, appendConfigurationEntry derives the next membership from that stale base (raft.go 1204-1241, configuration.go 224-302) once the admission gate sees latest==committed (raft.go 654-664). (6) 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8: with A's configuration coming from a snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry, AddVoter E returned no error and the silently created two-server change committed at index 11 with A's commit index at 11 and E holding the same LogConfiguration entry (parsed index 2), while B stayed at log index 10 with the old membership; the old majority {B,C} then elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, a_still_leader=true), and after the partition healed A's entry 11 was a LogNoop of term 4 rather than the committed configuration entry (parsed index 4, committed_entry_truncated=true). Receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c from the corrected harness scored both comparisons: entry at index 11 truncated after heal (violated, witness index 4) and a_still_leader=true while the old side elected B in term 4 (violated, witness index 3), with the silent change itself at index 2 (change_err nil, committed=true, LogConfiguration on A and E, B at log index 10). The repeat receipt 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e reproduced the same outcome under schedule variation (setup catch-up indices differed: C ended at log index 8 instead of 9): silent change committed at index 11 with entry type LogConfiguration on A and E (index 2), B elected in term 4 while A still led in term 3 (index 3, comparison violated), and the entry truncated after healing (index 4, comparison violated). Receipt e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064 (extended harness) scores both comparisons violated with witness index 5: the entry at the created index is truncated after healing, and after a client command returned success and was acknowledged and committed on the {A,B,E} leader (parsed index 3: write_applied=true, applied_a=12, fsm_a_logs=6) the FSM contents differ afterwards (fsm_a_logs=6 versus fsm_b_logs=5), so the client-visible effect survives only on the node whose log lost the entry. Summary of the current account for this question: the trigger is RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, a log whose newest configuration entry is at or below the persisted commit index, and no snapshot whose ConfigurationIndex covers that entry. Under that trigger the restarted node reconstructs its configuration only from the snapshot, so three consequence classes follow, each with retained control-backed receipts: (a) a missing membership context - empty configuration when there is no snapshot, which stops all campaigns and leaves a live quorum unable to elect (receipts 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc, 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a, 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837); (b) decisions taken from a stale base - a single AddVoter becomes the two-server change {A,B,C}->{A,B,E}, which silently drops a voter, and with a partitioned old voter produces concurrent leaders over the same log, truncation of the entry the stale leader had committed and divergent FSM state (receipts d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740, 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c, 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e and e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064); (c) stale membership accounting - a resurrected removed voter or a forgotten added voter makes the leader accept writes that the configuration committed in the log has not acknowledged (receipts 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 with 7adf927d528b4a74942c03b155aa8557, and b1daa1f4c9444b8d857bc7e0ab761691 with ec2c61af79bd42d7a5fe00657b7aeb22). Boundary: a snapshot covering the newest configuration entry, or leaving the flag at its default, removes every one of these observations in the controls, and once the stale configuration is adopted nothing re-reads the log for configurations, so it persists until one of three events repairs it: a snapshot is installed (the configuration comes from the snapshot metadata), a later configuration entry reaches the node through appendEntries and is processed by processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1569-1578, which installs the full membership the leader computed), or the node is restarted without the flag. In the empty-configuration cases the first two repairs need a leader, which is exactly what the empty configuration prevents. A repeat of the simultaneous-restart experiment reproduced the same failure and control values, so the headline progress claim also rests on two scored executions. A fourth consequence direction belongs to the client contracts: on the same stale leader, VerifyLeader confirms leadership from the stale quorum while a different majority of the committed configuration elects a leader in a higher term (receipt 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903, witness index 6), so the read-safety protection clients rely on is not effective in that state.

9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by retained receipt d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740: the restarted node adopts the snapshot-carried configuration when the newest configuration entry lies inside the replayed committed prefix (comparison 0 violated, witness index 1: servers_after=2 while the peer reports 3 and the newest configuration entry index 8 is below the staged commit index 11), and that stale base changes a real decision (comparison 2 violated, witness index 3: AddVoter E returned no error and both nodes ended with 3 members and contains_c_final=false, so voter C was silently removed). The same receipt's control mode kept 3 members and ended with 4 including C (observed at parsed index 5; that comparison was scored unknown because both modes shared a result event name, which the dedicated control experiment has now replaced with a scored holds).

a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-gap-1.explanation: Partly answered by source and receipt trace, not yet executed. The obvious route cannot work: a voter that never receives the silently-created {A,B,E} entry is strictly behind in the log, and the log up-to-date check in requestVote/requestPreVote (raft.go 1731-1746, 1812-1828) makes any voter that holds the entry refuse to vote for it, so the removed voter C cannot win alone or with a lagging peer. A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

1ed9540f22fe4fa9bef3b3bda88e22e8-gap-2.explanation: Resolved by retained receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c (scored): the silent two-server change {A,B,C} -> {A,B,E} committed on A plus the promoted caught-up nonvoter E (parsed index 2: change_err nil, x_index 11, committed=true, entry type LogConfiguration on A and on E, A commit index 11, B still at log index 10); the old majority {B,C} elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, comparison violated with witness 3), i.e. two concurrent leaders with disjoint support over the same log; and after healing, A's entry at index 11 became a LogNoop of term 4 (parsed index 4, comparison violated with witness 4), so the entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs was truncated on the node that had committed it. The earlier receipt 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8 reproduced the same observations but its comparisons were unscored because of my identity wiring; it is retained as the superseded revision of the same harness.

counterevidence: The isolated control receipt edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d scores holds with the identical restart and no snapshot (servers_after=1), so the loss is caused by replaying the committed prefix, not by restart, snapshot absence, or the commit-tracking store.

The snapshot run inside the first receipt (index 5) keeps the configuration, so the defect requires the newest configuration entry to be inside the skipped prefix; a snapshot taken after the change masks it.
Voter C never runs in the two-voter probe, so nothing in the receipts shows C resisting or noticing its removal; the claim is about the configuration the running nodes decide with.

The cluster-wide receipt 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a scores the control comparison holds (index 3, nodes_with_full_config=3) and the failing case violated (index 1, nodes_with_full_config=0), so the empty configuration after a simultaneous restart is specific to the replayed committed prefix.

Receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837 scores the control comparison holds (index 3: the two live voters re-elect a leader without the flag) and the failing case violated (index 1: after the configured voter stops, no leader among the two live voters although both hold every committed entry, log last index 13 on both), so the loss of electability is tied to the missing configuration rather than to the restart or the shutdown.

The dual-majority path needs a caught-up nonvoter E so the silent change can commit without the partitioned voter B; without such a node the change would need B's acknowledgement and B would then hold the new membership.

Two independent executions of the corrected dual-majority experiment (receipts 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c and 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e) produced the same entry index, the same concurrent leadership and the same truncation, so the outcome is reproducible rather than a single-run timing artifact.

In that extended execution the stale leader had already stepped down when the old side's leader was sampled (index 4, a_still_leader=false), which is why leader concurrency is reported as an observed window from the two earlier executions rather than as a comparison in the current harness.

Repeat receipt c1dcda29549b48c7a775adfc2e9a4bda reproduced the simultaneous-restart outcome exactly (servers_after [0,0,0], nodes_with_full_config 0, no leader in the observation window; control [3,3,3] with a leader elected at index 3), so the cluster-wide progress loss is reproducible under schedule variation (the staged commit indices differed from the first run: [11 10 11] against [11 11 9]).

Repeat receipt e0ef28c2bc89481aa6b3af478422de7c reproduced all three modes of the original probe with the same values: with RestoreCommittedLogs and no snapshot the node returns with an empty configuration and does not lead again (index 1), while the non-replay mode keeps its configuration and leads (index 3) and the snapshot mode keeps its configuration and leads (index 5).

Repeat receipt 2963a0b01d97404dbf946e7b87a214f8 reproduced the partial-restart outcome exactly (two restarted voters with empty configurations, the untouched voter leading at index 2 with nodes_with_full=1, then no leader among the two live voters holding log index 13 apiece; control re-electing at index 0), so the live-quorum progress loss is reproducible as well.

The revised dual-majority execution (receipt 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903) scored all three comparisons as predicted: the committed entry is truncated after healing (violated, witness 7), the FSMs diverge after an acknowledged write (violated, witness 7, fsm_a_logs 6 against fsm_b_logs 5), and the stale leader confirmed leadership while the old majority led in a higher term (violated, witness 6: verify_ok true, old_leader B in term 4, a_still_leader true).

The repeat of the client-contract revision (receipt 108a83830e904d90a9236738033c2c74) reproduced all three comparison outcomes (truncation violated at witness 7, FSM divergence violated at witness 7, confirmation-while-another-leader violated at witness 6 with verify_ok true, old_leader B in term 4 and A still leading), so that consequence is reproducible.
limitations: All executions are in-process in-memory clusters at protocol version 3 with 50ms heartbeat/election timeouts and a single committed configuration change; joint-consensus or multi-step changes are not exercised.
The finding is specific to RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag disabled the same durable state recovers normally in every receipt.

The configuration-less nodes still act as voters in other respects (they granted the configured voter's election win in receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837, index 0), which is why the cluster survived until that voter stopped; this is read from the receipt and from the membership checks being skipped for an empty configuration (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).

In that probe the partitioned side elects its leader with 3s election timeouts (reloaded to keep the restarted leader from losing the first election), so the interval is seconds; the ordering it demonstrates does not depend on those particular values.

The dual-majority probe has no control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter is a single-server change and cannot create disjoint majorities (nextConfiguration over the current configuration, configuration.go 224-302).

Leader concurrency on the two sides was observed with A still leading in four executions (receipts 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c, 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e, 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903 and 108a83830e904d90a9236738033c2c74) while one revision of the harness observed A already stepped down when the old side's leader was sampled, so the window is real but its length is schedule-dependent; the reproducible consequences are the truncation of the committed entry and the resulting FSM divergence.

The child question is now established by retained receipt 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 (resurrected membership and a write applied on the leader with B, required by the committed configuration, never receiving the entry; control refuses the same write), so the parents' consequence list includes premature commitment under a stale membership.

Two consequences reached by later receipts are no longer pending: the cluster-wide and partial-restart progress losses (receipts 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a and 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837) and the premature-commit-under-a-stale-membership consequence (receipt 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 with its repeat 7adf927d528b4a74942c03b155aa8557).

A source check of which snapshot the library considers newest found the expected protection: SnapshotStore implementations rank candidates by term then index (file_snapshot.go 535-547 with List at 286), so the newest snapshot is selected; no evidence of a snapshot-selection defect was found, and none is claimed.

The third consequence direction is now established by retained receipt b1daa1f4c9444b8d857bc7e0ab761691: a restarted leader that forgets an added voter accepted a write held by only two of the four committed voters, while the control refused it.

A check of the captured documentation found no statement about this feature outside the source: RestoreCommittedLogs and CommitTrackingLogStore appear only in config.go, log.go and api.go, and never in README.md, docs/README.md, docs/apply.md, docs/divergence.md, membership.md or CHANGELOG.md (those files do mention snapshots elsewhere, so the search itself is sound). The only normative text is the Config field comment, which requires the commit-tracking store but nothing about snapshots or configuration recovery, so no documented caller duty defeats the premise.

In the original probe and its repeat the two control modes share the comparison event names with the failing mode, so their comparisons are scored unknown; the scored control for the non-replay restart comes from the separate isolated-control experiment (receipt edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d, holds).

Correction of the repair-path statement: an earlier version of the summary said only a snapshot install or an operator restart repairs a stale configuration. A later configuration entry does too, because appendEntries processes new configuration entries and installs the membership encoded in them (raft.go 1569-1578); the three repair paths are now stated explicitly. This correction does not change any comparison or receipt; it narrows the persistence claim.

Receipt 8f0b76d0cd49441c81ecb603f1fcd527 is a build failure of the superseded revision of the partial-restart harness (undefined helpers declared in a sibling file) and is retained as a setup failure that carries no evidence; the partial-restart observations cited here come from the corrected revision's receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837 only. My repeat request named the superseded experiment revision rather than its correction, which is what produced that failure.

The client-contract consequence is now established by retained receipt 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903: VerifyLeader returned success on the stale-membership leader (its own acknowledgement plus the promoted voter's) in the same execution in which the old majority elected B in term 4 while that leader still considered itself leader, so the documented protection against returning stale data does not hold in this state.

The repair path through a later configuration entry is source-established (raft.go 1569-1578) and a construction-time run of the extended forgotten-added-voter harness reached it: with the stale leader stopped, the correctly configured side elected its own leader (B), that leader's AddVoter E succeeded, and the restarted stale node ended with five servers including the previously forgotten D and the new E. Its retained receipt is requested in this update.
interpretations.joint_history: All receipts belong to this question and were executed from the same snapshot. 430d7ba6 (empty configuration), d2d1cb09 (stale configuration and the silently dropped voter), edfd3c20 (isolated control, holds), 4f4a771f (all voters restart, cluster-wide progress loss), 7afe8c04 (live quorum cannot elect) and 79d93a5a (silent two-server change, concurrent leaders, truncation of the committed entry) form one chain: each was built from the previous receipt's outcome, and each uses the same bootstrap/commit/snapshot/restart operations rather than fabricated state.

interpretations.rationale: Two retained receipts. ee57ec0448704270bcbc1cf7ace9a045 established the membership half (restarted leader lists the removed voter C: three servers and two peers against B's two servers and one peer) but did not reach the write observation because B won the post-restart election. The corrected harness 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 scores all four comparisons as predicted: the resurrected membership (violated, witness index 1), the control keeping two servers (holds, index 5), the premature commit (violated, witness index 3: write_applied=true, entry_index 10, A commit and applied index 10, B's log still at 9, entry_on_quorum=false), and the control refusing the same write under the committed membership (holds, index 7, 'leadership lost while committing log'). Source: with Servers still containing C, the commitment installed on append (raft.go 1236-1241) makes A+C a quorum of the stale {A,B,C}, while the configuration committed in the log is {A,B} (quorum 2, both members), and the leader applies what it believes committed.
counterevidence: The control mode shows the same cluster, partition and stores refusing the write ('leadership lost while committing log') when the leader's configuration is the committed one, so the premature commit is attributable to the stale membership and not to the partition alone.

Repeat receipt 7adf927d528b4a74942c03b155aa8557 reproduced the identical comparison outcomes (resurrection violated at index 1, premature commit violated at index 3, control holds at index 7), so the observation is reproducible rather than a timing accident of the first corrected execution.
limitations: The partition is an explicit transport disconnection between A and B; the removed voter C is up and caught up, which is required for A to see a quorum in its stale view.

The repeat execution reproduced the same values and outcomes under the same setup (entry index 10, A commit and applied 10, B at 9, control refusing the write), so the premature-commit observation is not a single-run artifact.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts come from the same question and the same cluster construction (bootstrap {A,B,C} on A, snapshot, C offline for its removal, committed RemoveServer, further commits, restart of the leader on the same stores, C brought back on the same stores). ee57ec04 is the first revision of the harness; 226f9762 is its corrected successor, which differs only in keeping the stale leader in power, reporting whether it leads before the partition, and taking the compared index from the Apply future. The membership observation is common to both, so the earlier receipt remains a valid independent witness for it, while the write observation is taken only from the corrected revision where it was actually reached.

interpretations.rationale: Retained receipt b1daa1f4c9444b8d857bc7e0ab761691 scores all four comparisons as predicted. After a committed AddVoter D and a restart with RestoreCommittedLogs, the leader reports three servers and no longer contains D while the other three nodes report four (comparison 0 violated, witness index 1). With C and D disconnected, a single Apply on that leader succeeds: it commits and applies the entry at index 8 while C's log ends at 7 and D's at 6, so only two of the four committed voters hold it and the entry is not committed under the configuration in the log, which requires three (comparison 2 violated, witness index 3, voters_holding_entry=2, entry_on_committed_quorum=false). The controls hold: the same restart without the flag keeps four servers (index 5) and the same partition makes the write fail with 'leadership lost while committing log' (index 7). Mechanism: the in-memory configuration drives the quorum (configurationChangeChIfStable admits changes on stale indexes, appendConfigurationEntry derives membership from the stale base, commitment is installed from it on append), so a configuration missing a committed voter understates the quorum and lets the client be told a write succeeded.
counterevidence: The control mode on identical stores and the identical partition refuses the write, so the acceptance is attributable to the understated membership rather than to the partition.

Repeat receipt ec2c61af79bd42d7a5fe00657b7aeb22 scored the identical outcomes (membership violated at index 1, premature commit violated at index 3, controls hold at indices 5 and 7), so the observation is reproducible.
limitations: The example uses four voters; the size of the understatement grows with the number of voters added after the snapshot, so this probe understates rather than overstates the margin.

The repeat execution reproduced the same values and outcomes (leader with three servers while the others have four, entry index 8 applied on A with C at 7 and D at 6, control refusing the write), so the understated-quorum observation is not a single-run artifact.

scope.description: Same four-node scenario as the executed revision (A bootstrapped with {A,B,C}, snapshot, AddVoter D committed, further commits, A restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs so its configuration is the snapshot's {A,B,C}, B and C and D partitioned so a write lands on only two of four voters), extended with a repair phase: the stale leader A is shut down, B, C and D are reconnected and their timeouts shortened, one of them is elected, that leader appends AddVoter E, A is restarted again on its own stores with the flag still enabled, and the probe waits for the leader to replicate the new configuration entry to A and records A's resulting configuration.
assumptions: The repair phase is only meaningful for the failing mode, so it runs with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and is skipped in the control mode.
The leader from the correctly configured side can append a configuration change because its membership is the committed one ({A,B,C,D}, quorum three, with A down and the other three reachable).
A is restarted with a fresh transport wired to B, C and D, so the leader can replicate to it exactly as it would after an operator restart.
excluded: No snapshot is installed in the repair phase; the repair observed here is the log-entry path only.
The control mode runs without the repair phase, so its earlier comparisons keep their meaning.

Nothing is fabricated.

Control: with the committed membership the same partition must make the leader refuse the write.

scope.description: In-process single-voter Cluster: bootstrap a configuration entry, become leader, apply five commands, then restart the node on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore with a fresh transport. Three cases: restore_committed_logs on with no snapshot; off with no snapshot; on with a snapshot taken before the restart. Observations are the node's configuration size (GetConfiguration), whether it reaches Leader again, applied/commit indices, and staged commit index at restart.
assumptions: RestoreCommittedLogs is a documented public Config field (config.go 243-254) that is enabled by the application; the probe only supplies that documented configuration.
The existing test TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs always snapshots before restarting (raft_test.go 1183-1280), so the configuration-in-log path is not covered by it.
No snapshot is taken in the no-snapshot cases (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 10m), which is normal operation for clusters below the snapshot threshold.
excluded: Multi-node clusters and network partitions: the probe is a single-voter cluster, so the observed election abort is a progress loss and the vote-check consequence is source-read, not executed here.

basis.prefix: Fresh in-memory transport, InmemCommitTrackingStore log store, InmemStore stable store, InmemSnapshotStore; BootstrapCluster writes the single-voter configuration at index 1/term 1; first NewRaft elects the node as leader; five Apply commands are committed; optional user snapshot; Shutdown; second NewRaft on the same stores with a new transport sharing the same address. The harness never fabricates log entries or configuration state: all durable state comes from real bootstrap, real elections, real commits and a real snapshot.

comparisons.description: With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, the restarted node must still report the bootstrapped voter.
Control: the same restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the configuration, isolating the committed-prefix replay as the cause.

Control: with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a snapshot that carries the configuration, the restarted node keeps the configuration, showing that the loss is specific to configurations that only exist in the skipped committed log prefix.

scope.description: Two-voter in-memory cluster {A,B}: A is bootstrapped with both voters and becomes leader, commands are committed, A takes a snapshot (configuration {A,B} at index 1), then AddVoter C commits a configuration entry at index 8 while A and B are the only running servers. Four further commands push the persisted commit index past index 8. A is shut down and restarted on the same stores with a fresh transport (case restore_on with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, control restore_off with it false). Observed: the restarted node's configuration membership versus the still-running peer's view and the newest configuration entry in its own log; then, while the restarted node is stably leader, one further AddVoter E and the resulting cluster configuration on both nodes.
assumptions: AddVoter C commits with acks from A and B only, which is a legal quorum of three voters; C is never started, so nothing else can observe C's absence.
The snapshot predates the configuration change, so it carries configuration {A,B} at index 1 while the newest configuration entry (index 8) is in the log.
The extra commands after the change are ordinary applications; they only advance the persisted commit index past the configuration entry, which any later commit would do.
excluded: Elections, partitions and failover among more than two servers are not exercised; the point is which configuration each node uses, not how leaders are chosen.

basis.prefix: Real bootstrap of both voters on A, real election, real applies, real user snapshot on A, real AddVoter C through the cluster, real shutdown and restart of A on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore. Nothing is fabricated: the log, snapshot metadata and staged commit index all come from those operations, and the control case runs the identical procedure with RestoreCommittedLogs=false.

comparisons.description: After restart with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, the node must still know the newest committed configuration {A,B,C} that is present in its own log.
Control: the same restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps all three members.
A configuration change issued by the restarted node must not remove voter C, which no request removed and which remains in the committed configuration.

scope.description: Isolated control for the committed-log-replay finding: bootstrap a single voter, become leader, commit five commands, never snapshot (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 10m), shut down and restart on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore with RestoreCommittedLogs left at its default false. Emits only the control setup event and the control result event, so the control is scored independently of the failing mode.
assumptions: RestoreCommittedLogs defaults to false (config.go), so this is the ordinary restart path with identical durable state and identical missing snapshot.
The stores and the bootstrap/commit sequence are the same as in the failing probe, so the only difference is the replay of committed logs at startup.
excluded: No multi-voter cluster, no configuration change, no partitions.

basis.prefix: Real bootstrap, real election, real applies, real shutdown and restart on the same durable stores with a fresh transport; no fabricated log entries or configuration state.

comparisons.description: Control expectation: without replaying committed logs, the restarted node keeps its bootstrapped configuration, isolating the replay as the cause of the loss observed with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled.

scope.description: Three-voter in-memory cluster {A,B,C} bootstrapped on A, all three running and converged on the configuration, ten commands committed, no snapshot ever taken (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 10m). All three voters are then shut down and restarted at once on their own durable stores with fresh transports: case restore_on with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, control restore_off with it false. Observations: each node's configuration size (GetConfiguration), the number of nodes still holding the full configuration, and whether any leader is elected within a six-second opportunity (configured election/heartbeat timeouts are 50ms, so dozens of election windows).
assumptions: Every voter shares the same durable history because A bootstrapped and replicated it; all three stores report a persisted commit index at or above the configuration entry index before the restart (observed: [11 11 9] against the configuration entry at index 1).
No node snapshots before the restart, which is ordinary operation below SnapshotThreshold (8192 by default; the captured default SnapshotInterval is 120s).
Simultaneous restart of all voters is a legal operator action, not a fault injection: every node is stopped gracefully and started with its documented configuration.
excluded: No partitions, no disk faults, no message loss; the only varying factor is RestoreCommittedLogs.
The election fan-out itself is not traced beyond the observable absence of a leader and the logged 'no known peers, aborting election' path that source-reading identifies.

basis.prefix: Real bootstrap of all three voters on A's stores, real replication to B and C, real election, real applies, graceful shutdown of all three, then restart of all three on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances with fresh in-memory transports. Nothing is fabricated: configuration, log and commit index all come from those operations; the control case repeats the identical procedure with RestoreCommittedLogs=false.

comparisons.description: After a simultaneous restart with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, all three voters must still know the configuration whose entry is present in their own committed logs.
Control: the same simultaneous restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps all three voters configured, isolating the committed-prefix replay as the cause.

scope.description: Three-voter in-memory cluster {A,B,C} bootstrapped on A, converged, ten commands committed, no snapshot. Only voters A and B are restarted (case restore_on with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, control restore_off with it false) while C keeps running; the restarted voters' fresh transports are wired to each other and to C's live transport in both directions. The probe first observes which node leads (C, the only one still holding the configuration, is expected to win with votes from the configuration-less restarted voters), then stops that configured voter and observes whether the two remaining live voters - a quorum of three, each holding every committed entry (log last index 13 on both) - can elect a leader within six seconds at 50ms timeouts.
assumptions: Restarting two voters while one keeps running is the ordinary rolling/cold restart an operator may perform; all three stores already contain the bootstrapped configuration entry and every committed entry.
The decision to stop the configured voter afterwards is a normal availability event (the node is gracefully shut down), not a fault injection: two of three voters remain alive and up to date.
A quorum of two live voters with complete logs is entitled to elect a leader in this cluster, which is exactly what the control case measures.
excluded: No partitions, no disk faults, no message loss, no injected delays.
The election fan-out to the stopped node is not traced; the observation is the absence of any leader among the live voters.

experiments.revision_reason: The previous invocation of this probe failed before any test ran (receipt ece1e96fdfc74eefadb2bd4c1c62b52b, exit 1, 'Package discovery, build or dependency preparation failed'): the harness used helper functions that were declared in the sibling harness file of the earlier cluster-wide probe, and only the named harness file is copied into the captured package. Every helper is now declared inside this harness and the probe was re-verified in an isolated copy of the captured tree containing only this harness, so the comparison basis and predictions are unchanged.

scope.description: Four in-process nodes at protocol version 3 with 300ms heartbeat/election/lease: A and B are bootstrapped as voters {A,B}; A snapshots, adds E as a caught-up nonvoter, adds C as a voter (config {A,B,C} plus nonvoter E), commits four commands. A is shut down and restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true so its in-memory configuration comes from the snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry; the other three nodes get longer timeouts so the restarted leader wins back leadership. B is then partitioned from A (C is already absent from A's stale configuration, so A replicates to nobody but E), and A issues one AddVoter E. Observations: whether that change commits and with whose acknowledgement, each side's configuration and log tail, who leads each side and in which term, and the content of A's log at the created entry index before and after the partition is healed.
assumptions: E is a caught-up nonvoter before the change, which is what lets the silently-created {A,B,E} configuration commit with A and E alone once B is partitioned; this is ordinary use of AddNonvoter followed by AddVoter.
Restarting the leader with RestoreCommittedLogs=true is the documented configuration already established by the earlier receipts; nothing else about the cluster changes.
The partition is applied by disconnecting the in-memory transports in both directions, which is a real partition for all Raft traffic (AppendEntries, heartbeats, votes).
Both sides keep following the protocol: A leads the {A,B,E} configuration with E's acknowledgements, and B and C campaign under their own {A,B,C} configuration after their election timeout.
excluded: No control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter adds a single server and the two-server change cannot arise; that is a source-level statement (nextConfiguration over the current configuration) rather than an execution.
No disk faults or message loss; the only partition is the one applied explicitly.

experiments.revision_reason: The executed run reproduced every observation but both comparisons were scored unknown because the identity field I declared (x_index) was absent from the result events and the prerequisite event could therefore not be correlated to them. The harness now emits x_index in old_side_elected and after_heal, so the admission on silent_change (committed, entry_type_at_x=LogConfiguration) correlates with both result events; predictions, scope and prefix are unchanged, and the corrected harness was re-verified in an isolated copy of the captured tree.

scope.description: Four in-process nodes at protocol version 3 with 300ms heartbeat/election/lease: A and B bootstrapped as voters {A,B}; A snapshots, adds E as a caught-up nonvoter, adds C as a voter, commits four commands. A is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true so its configuration comes from the snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds {A,B,C}; B is partitioned; A issues AddVoter E, which the stale base turns into the two-server change {A,B,E} and which commits on A plus E. The probe then issues one client command on A (committed with A and E) and finally heals the partition, observing the entry at the created index and the FSM contents of A and of the old-majority leader.
assumptions: E is a caught-up nonvoter before the change, so {A,B,E} commits with A and E alone once B is partitioned.
The client command is an ordinary Apply on the leader that has a quorum of the configuration recorded in its own log ({A,B,E}: A and E).
MockFSM records one entry per LogCommand applied, so its length is the number of committed commands that node's FSM has consumed.
Both sides keep running the protocol; the partition is applied by disconnecting in-memory transports in both directions.
excluded: No control variant: with the flag disabled the configuration is current, so the same AddVoter is a single-server change and cannot create the disjoint majorities (nextConfiguration over the current configuration).
Leader concurrency is not asserted as a comparison here because its window depends on when the higher-term vote requests reach the stale leader.

experiments.revision_reason: The executed revision established the silent change and the truncation of the committed entry. This revision adds the client-facing observation of the same path: a client write issued on the {A,B,E} leader A after the silent change (committed with A and E) and the FSM contents of A and of the old-majority leader afterwards. It also drops the earlier 'at most one leader' comparison because a construction-time run of this revision observed A stepping down before the old side's leader was sampled (vote requests in the higher term reach A from the connected side), so the leader-concurrency window is schedule-dependent and is retained as an observation from the two scored executions rather than as a comparison in this harness.

scope.description: Three-voter in-process cluster {A,B,C} at protocol version 3 with 50ms timeouts. A snapshots, then C is shut down for its own removal, RemoveServer C commits with {A,B}, two further commands push the persisted commit index past the removal entry, and A is restarted on the same stores with RestoreCommittedLogs (case restore_on) or without it (control restore_off). The restarted A's configuration and peer count are observed against B's. Then C is brought back on its old stores so it catches up from A, B is partitioned from A, and one Apply is issued on A; the probe records whether the Apply succeeded, the entry index, A's commit and applied indexes, whether the entry reached B, and the FSM lengths on both sides.
assumptions: C is offline for its own removal, so it never learns it was removed; that is an ordinary operator sequence (a failed node is removed while down and then comes back).
B and C both hold every entry up to the removal, so the entries, commit index and configurations come from real replication.
After the partition, {A,B} is the configuration committed in the log (removal entry committed), so an entry present only on A cannot be committed.
excluded: No disk faults or message loss; the only partition is the explicit disconnection of B.
The probe does not assert what happens after the partition heals, which is the subject of the dual-majority harness.

interpretations.rationale: NewRaft documents that existing state such as logs and peers is restored (api.go 504-507) and RestoreCommittedLogs is documented only as replaying committed logs before startup (config.go 243-254); nothing waives configuration recovery. The code nevertheless bounds the configuration scan by max(lastSnapshot, lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613) while restoreFromCommittedLogs has already raised lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755). processConfigurationLogEntry is the only path that turns a log entry into r.configurations (raft.go 1605-1623), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are dropped whenever a snapshot does not carry them (snapshot path: api.go 645-689). Consequence: after a plain restart of a bootstrapped node with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, r.configurations.latest is empty, so runFollower refuses to campaign ('no known peers', raft.go 230-234) and both requestVote and requestPreVote skip their membership checks because they are gated on a non-empty Servers list (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784). The rule that decides the decision is therefore evaluated against an empty configuration rather than the replicated one.
counterevidence: The existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs (raft_test.go 1183-1280) passes: it always snapshots before restarting, so its configuration comes from snapshot metadata rather than from the log, and the same probe shows that a snapshot-carried configuration masks the loss.

The loss is not caused by the commit-tracking store or by replaying logs to the FSM per se: the control restart with RestoreCommittedLogs=false on identical stores and log contents keeps the configuration and wins the election again.
limitations: The executed probe is a single-voter in-memory cluster; the multi-node consequences (a node that grants votes to servers it cannot be shown to contain, or a node whose quorum size is computed from a stale configuration) are read from source, not executed.

The persisted commit index used at restart is what the store reported (6 while the log ended at 7); the drop of the configuration entry does not depend on that lag, but the exact boundary of what is skipped does.
Whether upstream intends applications to always snapshot before enabling this option is not stated anywhere in the captured sources; the Config documentation mentions no such requirement.

interpretations.rationale: Observed in the retained execution: after restart with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot, the node's configuration is empty (event index 1: mode=restore_on_no_snapshot, servers_before=1, servers_after=0, config_preserved=false, snapshot_count=0, staged_commit=6, log_last_index=7) and it never campaigns again (became_leader=false after a 3s opportunity, with the node logging 'no known peers, aborting election'), while the two controls keep the configuration and re-elect (index 3 restore_off_no_snapshot: servers_after=1, became_leader=true; index 5 restore_on_with_snapshot: servers_after=1, snapshot_count=1, became_leader=true). Source account of the mechanism: NewRaft documents that existing state such as logs and peers is restored (api.go 504-507) and RestoreCommittedLogs is documented only as replaying committed logs before startup (config.go 243-254); restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755) and the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never turned into r.configurations by their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). The node still has all committed entries on disk (log_last_index=7 > commit_index=6), so this is a lost configuration context, not lost data; the entry itself is present and would be re-read only if a snapshot were installed.
limitations: Executed scope is a single-voter in-memory cluster (protocol version 3, heartbeat/election 50ms); the multi-node consequences (votes granted to servers the node cannot show it contains, quorum size and configuration changes computed from a stale base) are read from source and are the subject of the registered gap.
The restart uses the commit index the store reported (6, log end 7); the boundary of the skipped prefix depends on that value, but the omission of the configuration entry does not.

The obvious route cannot work: a voter that never receives the silently-created {A,B,E} entry is strictly behind in the log, and the log up-to-date check in requestVote/requestPreVote (raft.go 1731-1746, 1812-1828) makes any voter that holds the entry refuse to vote for it, so the removed voter C cannot win alone or with a lagging peer. A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-gap-1.explanation: Partly answered by source and receipt trace, not yet executed. Boundary: a snapshot covering the newest configuration entry, or leaving the flag at its default, removes every one of these observations in the controls, and once the stale configuration is adopted nothing re-reads the log for configurations, so it persists until one of three events repairs it: a snapshot is installed (the configuration comes from the snapshot metadata), a later configuration entry reaches the node through appendEntries and is processed by processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1569-1578, which installs the full membership the leader computed), or the node is restarted without the flag. In the empty-configuration cases the first two repairs need a leader, which is exactly what the empty configuration prevents. A repeat of the simultaneous-restart experiment reproduced the same failure and control values, so the headline progress claim also rests on two scored executions.

9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by retained receipt d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740: the restarted node adopts the snapshot-carried configuration when the newest configuration entry lies inside the replayed committed prefix (comparison 0 violated, witness index 1: servers_after=2 while the peer reports 3 and the newest configuration entry index 8 is below the staged commit index 11), and that stale base changes a real decision (comparison 2 violated, witness index 3: AddVoter E returned no error and both nodes ended with 3 members and contains_c_final=false, so voter C was silently removed). The same receipt's control mode kept 3 members and ended with 4 including C (observed at parsed index 5; that comparison was scored unknown because both modes shared a result event name, which the dedicated control experiment has now replaced with a scored holds).

a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-gap-1.explanation: Partly answered by source and receipt trace, not yet executed. The obvious route cannot work: a voter that never receives the silently-created {A,B,E} entry is strictly behind in the log, and the log up-to-date check in requestVote/requestPreVote (raft.go 1731-1746, 1812-1828) makes any voter that holds the entry refuse to vote for it, so the removed voter C cannot win alone or with a lagging peer. A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

1ed9540f22fe4fa9bef3b3bda88e22e8-gap-2.explanation: Resolved by retained receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c (scored): the silent two-server change {A,B,C} -> {A,B,E} committed on A plus the promoted caught-up nonvoter E (parsed index 2: change_err nil, x_index 11, committed=true, entry type LogConfiguration on A and on E, A commit index 11, B still at log index 10); the old majority {B,C} elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, comparison violated with witness 3), i.e. two concurrent leaders with disjoint support over the same log; and after healing, A's entry at index 11 became a LogNoop of term 4 (parsed index 4, comparison violated with witness 4), so the entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs was truncated on the node that had committed it. Voter C never runs in the two-voter probe, so nothing in the receipts shows C resisting or noticing its removal; the claim is about the configuration the running nodes decide with.

(2) d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740 index 1: with a snapshot carrying {A,B}@1 and a committed AddVoter C at index 8 with staged commit 11, the restarted node reports 2 servers while its continuously running peer reports 3 and its own log still holds the newest configuration entry; index 3: a later AddVoter E then returns no error and both nodes converge on 3 members without C (contains_c_final=false), i.e. a legitimately added voter is silently removed from the cluster by a change computed from the stale base. interpretations.rationale: Three independent receipts, all retained. (1) 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc index 1: with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot the restarting node returns with an empty configuration (servers_after=0 against servers_before=1), never campaigns again in a 3s opportunity, and logs 'no known peers, aborting election'; both the non-replay run (index 3) and the snapshot run (index 5) keep the configuration and re-elect. (2) d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740 index 1: with a snapshot carrying {A,B}@1 and a committed AddVoter C at index 8 with staged commit 11, the restarted node reports 2 servers while its continuously running peer reports 3 and its own log still holds the newest configuration entry; index 3: a later AddVoter E then returns no error and both nodes converge on 3 members without C (contains_c_final=false), i.e. a legitimately added voter is silently removed from the cluster by a change computed from the stale base. (3) edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d index 1: the isolated control with RestoreCommittedLogs=false scores holds (servers_after=1 against the same bootstrapped voter), so the replayed committed prefix, not restart itself, is the cause. (4) 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a index 1: restarting all three voters at once with the flag leaves servers_after=[0,0,0] and nodes_with_full_config=0 with no leader in a six-second opportunity, while the same procedure without the flag scores holds at index 3 (nodes_with_full_config=3, leader elected) - a cluster-wide progress loss, not a single node's lost context. (5) 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837: with only two of three voters restarted, the untouched configured voter leads with the configuration-less nodes' votes (index 0, servers_after=[0,0,3]); once that voter stops, the two remaining live, fully up-to-date voters cannot elect a leader in six seconds at 50ms timeouts (index 1, log last index 13 on both), while the control without the flag re-elects immediately (index 3).
