With Servers empty the follower refuses to campaign (raft.go 230-234 on every heartbeat timeout, raft.go 214-251) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784); with Servers stale, appendConfigurationEntry derives the next membership from that stale base (raft.go 1204-1241, configuration.go 224-302) once the admission gate sees latest==committed (raft.go 654-664). (6) 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8: with A's configuration coming from a snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry, AddVoter E returned no error and the silently created two-server change committed at index 11 with A's commit index at 11 and E holding the same LogConfiguration entry (parsed index 2), while B stayed at log index 10 with the old membership; the old majority {B,C} then elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, a_still_leader=true), and after the partition healed A's entry 11 was a LogNoop of term 4 rather than the committed configuration entry (parsed index 4, committed_entry_truncated=true). Receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c from the corrected harness scored both comparisons: entry at index 11 truncated after heal (violated, witness index 4) and a_still_leader=true while the old side elected B in term 4 (violated, witness index 3), with the silent change itself at index 2 (change_err nil, committed=true, LogConfiguration on A and E, B at log index 10). The repeat receipt 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e reproduced the same outcome under schedule variation (setup catch-up indices differed: C ended at log index 8 instead of 9): silent change committed at index 11 with entry type LogConfiguration on A and E (index 2), B elected in term 4 while A still led in term 3 (index 3, comparison violated), and the entry truncated after healing (index 4, comparison violated). Receipt e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064 (extended harness) scores both comparisons violated with witness index 5: the entry at the created index is truncated after healing, and after a client command returned success and was acknowledged and committed on the {A,B,E} leader (parsed index 3: write_applied=true, applied_a=12, fsm_a_logs=6) the FSM contents differ afterwards (fsm_a_logs=6 versus fsm_b_logs=5), so the client-visible effect survives only on the node whose log lost the entry. Summary of the current account for this question: the trigger is RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, a log whose newest configuration entry is at or below the persisted commit index, and no snapshot whose ConfigurationIndex covers that entry. Under that trigger the restarted node reconstructs its configuration only from the snapshot, so three consequence classes follow, each with retained control-backed receipts: (a) a missing membership context - empty configuration when there is no snapshot, which stops all campaigns and leaves a live quorum unable to elect (receipts 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc, 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a, 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837); (b) decisions taken from a stale base - a single AddVoter becomes the two-server change {A,B,C}->{A,B,E}, which silently drops a voter, and with a partitioned old voter produces concurrent leaders over the same log, truncation of the entry the stale leader had committed and divergent FSM state (receipts d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740, 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c, 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e and e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064); (c) stale membership accounting - a resurrected removed voter or a forgotten added voter makes the leader accept writes that the configuration committed in the log has not acknowledged (receipts 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 with 7adf927d528b4a74942c03b155aa8557, and b1daa1f4c9444b8d857bc7e0ab761691 with ec2c61af79bd42d7a5fe00657b7aeb22). Boundary: a snapshot covering the newest configuration entry, or leaving the flag at its default, removes every one of these observations in the controls, and once the stale configuration is adopted nothing re-reads the log for configurations, so it persists until one of three events repairs it: a snapshot is installed (the configuration comes from the snapshot metadata), a later configuration entry reaches the node through appendEntries and is processed by processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1569-1578, which installs the full membership the leader computed), or the node is restarted without the flag. In the empty-configuration cases the first two repairs need a leader, which is exactly what the empty configuration prevents. A repeat of the simultaneous-restart experiment reproduced the same failure and control values, so the headline progress claim also rests on two scored executions.

9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by retained receipt d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740: the restarted node adopts the snapshot-carried configuration when the newest configuration entry lies inside the replayed committed prefix (comparison 0 violated, witness index 1: servers_after=2 while the peer reports 3 and the newest configuration entry index 8 is below the staged commit index 11), and that stale base changes a real decision (comparison 2 violated, witness index 3: AddVoter E returned no error and both nodes ended with 3 members and contains_c_final=false, so voter C was silently removed). The same receipt's control mode kept 3 members and ended with 4 including C (observed at parsed index 5; that comparison was scored unknown because both modes shared a result event name, which the dedicated control experiment has now replaced with a scored holds).

a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-gap-1.explanation: Partly answered by source and receipt trace, not yet executed. The obvious route cannot work: a voter that never receives the silently-created {A,B,E} entry is strictly behind in the log, and the log up-to-date check in requestVote/requestPreVote (raft.go 1731-1746, 1812-1828) makes any voter that holds the entry refuse to vote for it, so the removed voter C cannot win alone or with a lagging peer. A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

1ed9540f22fe4fa9bef3b3bda88e22e8-gap-2.explanation: Resolved by retained receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c (scored): the silent two-server change {A,B,C} -> {A,B,E} committed on A plus the promoted caught-up nonvoter E (parsed index 2: change_err nil, x_index 11, committed=true, entry type LogConfiguration on A and on E, A commit index 11, B still at log index 10); the old majority {B,C} elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, comparison violated with witness 3), i.e. two concurrent leaders with disjoint support over the same log; and after healing, A's entry at index 11 became a LogNoop of term 4 (parsed index 4, comparison violated with witness 4), so the entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs was truncated on the node that had committed it. The earlier receipt 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8 reproduced the same observations but its comparisons were unscored because of my identity wiring; it is retained as the superseded revision of the same harness.

counterevidence: The isolated control receipt edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d scores holds with the identical restart and no snapshot (servers_after=1), so the loss is caused by replaying the committed prefix, not by restart, snapshot absence, or the commit-tracking store.

The snapshot run inside the first receipt (index 5) keeps the configuration, so the defect requires the newest configuration entry to be inside the skipped prefix; a snapshot taken after the change masks it.
Voter C never runs in the two-voter probe, so nothing in the receipts shows C resisting or noticing its removal; the claim is about the configuration the running nodes decide with.

The cluster-wide receipt 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a scores the control comparison holds (index 3, nodes_with_full_config=3) and the failing case violated (index 1, nodes_with_full_config=0), so the empty configuration after a simultaneous restart is specific to the replayed committed prefix.

Receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837 scores the control comparison holds (index 3: the two live voters re-elect a leader without the flag) and the failing case violated (index 1: after the configured voter stops, no leader among the two live voters although both hold every committed entry, log last index 13 on both), so the loss of electability is tied to the missing configuration rather than to the restart or the shutdown.

The dual-majority path needs a caught-up nonvoter E so the silent change can commit without the partitioned voter B; without such a node the change would need B's acknowledgement and B would then hold the new membership.

Two independent executions of the corrected dual-majority experiment (receipts 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c and 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e) produced the same entry index, the same concurrent leadership and the same truncation, so the outcome is reproducible rather than a single-run timing artifact.

In that extended execution the stale leader had already stepped down when the old side's leader was sampled (index 4, a_still_leader=false), which is why leader concurrency is reported as an observed window from the two earlier executions rather than as a comparison in the current harness.

Repeat receipt c1dcda29549b48c7a775adfc2e9a4bda reproduced the simultaneous-restart outcome exactly (servers_after [0,0,0], nodes_with_full_config 0, no leader in the observation window; control [3,3,3] with a leader elected at index 3), so the cluster-wide progress loss is reproducible under schedule variation (the staged commit indices differed from the first run: [11 10 11] against [11 11 9]).

Repeat receipt e0ef28c2bc89481aa6b3af478422de7c reproduced all three modes of the original probe with the same values: with RestoreCommittedLogs and no snapshot the node returns with an empty configuration and does not lead again (index 1), while the non-replay mode keeps its configuration and leads (index 3) and the snapshot mode keeps its configuration and leads (index 5).

Repeat receipt 2963a0b01d97404dbf946e7b87a214f8 reproduced the partial-restart outcome exactly (two restarted voters with empty configurations, the untouched voter leading at index 2 with nodes_with_full=1, then no leader among the two live voters holding log index 13 apiece; control re-electing at index 0), so the live-quorum progress loss is reproducible as well.
limitations: All executions are in-process in-memory clusters at protocol version 3 with 50ms heartbeat/election timeouts and a single committed configuration change; joint-consensus or multi-step changes are not exercised.
The finding is specific to RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag disabled the same durable state recovers normally in every receipt.

The configuration-less nodes still act as voters in other respects (they granted the configured voter's election win in receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837, index 0), which is why the cluster survived until that voter stopped; this is read from the receipt and from the membership checks being skipped for an empty configuration (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).

In that probe the partitioned side elects its leader with 3s election timeouts (reloaded to keep the restarted leader from losing the first election), so the interval is seconds; the ordering it demonstrates does not depend on those particular values.

The dual-majority probe has no control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter is a single-server change and cannot create disjoint majorities (nextConfiguration over the current configuration, configuration.go 224-302).

Leader concurrency on the two sides was observed in the two scored executions (A still leader in term 3 while B led term 4) but a later construction-time run of the extended harness observed A already stepped down when the old side's leader was sampled, so that window is schedule-dependent; the reproducible consequences are the truncation of the committed entry and the resulting FSM divergence.

The child question is now established by retained receipt 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 (resurrected membership and a write applied on the leader with B, required by the committed configuration, never receiving the entry; control refuses the same write), so the parents' consequence list includes premature commitment under a stale membership.

Two consequences reached by later receipts are no longer pending: the cluster-wide and partial-restart progress losses (receipts 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a and 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837) and the premature-commit-under-a-stale-membership consequence (receipt 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 with its repeat 7adf927d528b4a74942c03b155aa8557).

A source check of which snapshot the library considers newest found the expected protection: SnapshotStore implementations rank candidates by term then index (file_snapshot.go 535-547 with List at 286), so the newest snapshot is selected; no evidence of a snapshot-selection defect was found, and none is claimed.

The third consequence direction is now established by retained receipt b1daa1f4c9444b8d857bc7e0ab761691: a restarted leader that forgets an added voter accepted a write held by only two of the four committed voters, while the control refused it.

A check of the captured documentation found no statement about this feature outside the source: RestoreCommittedLogs and CommitTrackingLogStore appear only in config.go, log.go and api.go, and never in README.md, docs/README.md, docs/apply.md, docs/divergence.md, membership.md or CHANGELOG.md (those files do mention snapshots elsewhere, so the search itself is sound). The only normative text is the Config field comment, which requires the commit-tracking store but nothing about snapshots or configuration recovery, so no documented caller duty defeats the premise.

In the original probe and its repeat the two control modes share the comparison event names with the failing mode, so their comparisons are scored unknown; the scored control for the non-replay restart comes from the separate isolated-control experiment (receipt edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d, holds).

Correction of the repair-path statement: an earlier version of the summary said only a snapshot install or an operator restart repairs a stale configuration. A later configuration entry does too, because appendEntries processes new configuration entries and installs the membership encoded in them (raft.go 1569-1578); the three repair paths are now stated explicitly. This correction does not change any comparison or receipt; it narrows the persistence claim.

Receipt 8f0b76d0cd49441c81ecb603f1fcd527 is a build failure of the superseded revision of the partial-restart harness (undefined helpers declared in a sibling file) and is retained as a setup failure that carries no evidence; the partial-restart observations cited here come from the corrected revision's receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837 only. My repeat request named the superseded experiment revision rather than its correction, which is what produced that failure.

The stale-membership consequence set now includes a client-contract observation being probed: on the same stale leader, VerifyLeader returned success (leadership confirmed with the acknowledgements of itself and the promoted voter) at the very time another majority elected a leader in a higher term, so the documented protection against stale reads does not hold in that state; its retained receipt is requested in this update.

interpretations.joint_history: All receipts belong to this question and were executed from the same snapshot. 430d7ba6 (empty configuration), d2d1cb09 (stale configuration and the silently dropped voter), edfd3c20 (isolated control, holds), 4f4a771f (all voters restart, cluster-wide progress loss), 7afe8c04 (live quorum cannot elect) and 79d93a5a (silent two-server change, concurrent leaders, truncation of the committed entry) form one chain: each was built from the previous receipt's outcome, and each uses the same bootstrap/commit/snapshot/restart operations rather than fabricated state.

interpretations.rationale: Three independent receipts, all retained. (1) 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc index 1: with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot the restarting node returns with an empty configuration (servers_after=0 against servers_before=1), never campaigns again in a 3s opportunity, and logs 'no known peers, aborting election'; both the non-replay run (index 3) and the snapshot run (index 5) keep the configuration and re-elect. (2) d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740 index 1: with a snapshot carrying {A,B}@1 and a committed AddVoter C at index 8 with staged commit 11, the restarted node reports 2 servers while its continuously running peer reports 3 and its own log still holds the newest configuration entry; index 3: a later AddVoter E then returns no error and both nodes converge on 3 members without C (contains_c_final=false), i.e. a legitimately added voter is silently removed from the cluster by a change computed from the stale base. (3) edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d index 1: the isolated control with RestoreCommittedLogs=false scores holds (servers_after=1 against the same bootstrapped voter), so the replayed committed prefix, not restart itself, is the cause. (4) 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a index 1: restarting all three voters at once with the flag leaves servers_after=[0,0,0] and nodes_with_full_config=0 with no leader in a six-second opportunity, while the same procedure without the flag scores holds at index 3 (nodes_with_full_config=3, leader elected) - a cluster-wide progress loss, not a single node's lost context. (5) 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837: with only two of three voters restarted, the untouched configured voter leads with the configuration-less nodes' votes (index 0, servers_after=[0,0,3]); once that voter stops, the two remaining live, fully up-to-date voters cannot elect a leader in six seconds at 50ms timeouts (index 1, log last index 13 on both), while the control without the flag re-elects immediately (index 3). Source chain: restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755); the configuration scan then begins at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never fed to their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). With Servers empty the follower refuses to campaign (raft.go 230-234 on every heartbeat timeout, raft.go 214-251) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784); with Servers stale, appendConfigurationEntry derives the next membership from that stale base (raft.go 1204-1241, configuration.go 224-302) once the admission gate sees latest==committed (raft.go 654-664). (6) 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8: with A's configuration coming from a snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry, AddVoter E returned no error and the silently created two-server change committed at index 11 with A's commit index at 11 and E holding the same LogConfiguration entry (parsed index 2), while B stayed at log index 10 with the old membership; the old majority {B,C} then elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, a_still_leader=true), and after the partition healed A's entry 11 was a LogNoop of term 4 rather than the committed configuration entry (parsed index 4, committed_entry_truncated=true). Receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c from the corrected harness scored both comparisons: entry at index 11 truncated after heal (violated, witness index 4) and a_still_leader=true while the old side elected B in term 4 (violated, witness index 3), with the silent change itself at index 2 (change_err nil, committed=true, LogConfiguration on A and E, B at log index 10). The repeat receipt 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e reproduced the same outcome under schedule variation (setup catch-up indices differed: C ended at log index 8 instead of 9): silent change committed at index 11 with entry type LogConfiguration on A and E (index 2), B elected in term 4 while A still led in term 3 (index 3, comparison violated), and the entry truncated after healing (index 4, comparison violated). Receipt e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064 (extended harness) scores both comparisons violated with witness index 5: the entry at the created index is truncated after healing, and after a client command returned success and was acknowledged and committed on the {A,B,E} leader (parsed index 3: write_applied=true, applied_a=12, fsm_a_logs=6) the FSM contents differ afterwards (fsm_a_logs=6 versus fsm_b_logs=5), so the client-visible effect survives only on the node whose log lost the entry. Summary of the current account for this question: the trigger is RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, a log whose newest configuration entry is at or below the persisted commit index, and no snapshot whose ConfigurationIndex covers that entry. Under that trigger the restarted node reconstructs its configuration only from the snapshot, so three consequence classes follow, each with retained control-backed receipts: (a) a missing membership context - empty configuration when there is no snapshot, which stops all campaigns and leaves a live quorum unable to elect (receipts 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc, 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a, 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837); (b) decisions taken from a stale base - a single AddVoter becomes the two-server change {A,B,C}->{A,B,E}, which silently drops a voter, and with a partitioned old voter produces concurrent leaders over the same log, truncation of the entry the stale leader had committed and divergent FSM state (receipts d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740, 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c, 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e and e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064); (c) stale membership accounting - a resurrected removed voter or a forgotten added voter makes the leader accept writes that the configuration committed in the log has not acknowledged (receipts 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 with 7adf927d528b4a74942c03b155aa8557, and b1daa1f4c9444b8d857bc7e0ab761691 with ec2c61af79bd42d7a5fe00657b7aeb22). Boundary: a snapshot covering the newest configuration entry, or leaving the flag at its default, removes every one of these observations in the controls, and once the stale configuration is adopted nothing re-reads the log for configurations, so it persists until one of three events repairs it: a snapshot is installed (the configuration comes from the snapshot metadata), a later configuration entry reaches the node through appendEntries and is processed by processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1569-1578, which installs the full membership the leader computed), or the node is restarted without the flag. In the empty-configuration cases the first two repairs need a leader, which is exactly what the empty configuration prevents. A repeat of the simultaneous-restart experiment reproduced the same failure and control values, so the headline progress claim also rests on two scored executions. A fourth consequence direction belongs to the client contracts: on the same stale leader, VerifyLeader confirms leadership from the stale quorum while a different majority of the committed configuration elects a leader in a higher term (receipt 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903, witness index 6), so the read-safety protection clients rely on is not effective in that state.

a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-gap-1.explanation: Partly answered by source and receipt trace, not yet executed. The obvious route cannot work: a voter that never receives the silently-created {A,B,E} entry is strictly behind in the log, and the log up-to-date check in requestVote/requestPreVote (raft.go 1731-1746, 1812-1828) makes any voter that holds the entry refuse to vote for it, so the removed voter C cannot win alone or with a lagging peer. A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

result.summary: Executed the one remaining open thread — the repair path I had only stated from source — by extending the forgotten-added-voter harness with a repair phase. In the construction-time run the stale leader was stopped, the correctly configured members reconnected and elected B, B's AddVoter E succeeded, and the stale node restarted on its own stores ended with five members including the previously forgotten D and the new E: a later configuration entry replicated by a correct leader does restore a stale node, which bounds the persistence claim I had corrected earlier. The revision is submitted as a successor of the current understate experiment with the four earlier comparisons preserved and one added (the repaired configuration must contain all five members); the interpretation replaces the source-only limitation with the construction-time result and marks its retained receipt as pending.

scope.description: In-process single-voter Cluster: bootstrap a configuration entry, become leader, apply five commands, then restart the node on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore with a fresh transport. Observations are the node's configuration size (GetConfiguration), whether it reaches Leader again, applied/commit indices, and staged commit index at restart.
assumptions: RestoreCommittedLogs is a documented public Config field (config.go 243-254) that is enabled by the application; the probe only supplies that documented configuration.

scope.description: Two-voter in-memory cluster {A,B}: A is bootstrapped with both voters and becomes leader, commands are committed, A takes a snapshot (configuration {A,B} at index 1), then AddVoter C commits a configuration entry at index 8 while A and B are the only running servers. Four further commands push the persisted commit index past index 8. A is shut down and restarted on the same stores with a fresh transport (case restore_on with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, control restore_off with it false). Observed: the restarted node's configuration membership versus the still-running peer's view and the newest configuration entry in its own log; then, while the restarted node is stably leader, one further AddVoter E and the resulting cluster configuration on both nodes.
assumptions: AddVoter C commits with acks from A and B only, which is a legal quorum of three voters; C is never started, so nothing else can observe C's absence.

The extra commands after the change are ordinary applications; they only advance the persisted commit index past the configuration entry, which any later commit would do.
excluded: Elections, partitions and failover among more than two servers are not exercised; the point is which configuration each node uses, not how leaders are chosen.

scope.description: Three-voter in-memory cluster {A,B,C} bootstrapped on A, all three running and converged on the configuration, ten commands committed, no snapshot ever taken (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 10m). assumptions: Every voter shares the same durable history because A bootstrapped and replicated it; all three stores report a persisted commit index at or above the configuration entry index before the restart (observed: [11 11 9] against the configuration entry at index 1).

excluded: No partitions, no disk faults, no message loss; the only varying factor is RestoreCommittedLogs.

scope.description: Three-voter in-memory cluster {A,B,C} bootstrapped on A, converged, ten commands committed, no snapshot. Only voters A and B are restarted (case restore_on with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, control restore_off with it false) while C keeps running; the restarted voters' fresh transports are wired to each other and to C's live transport in both directions. The probe first observes which node leads (C, the only one still holding the configuration, is expected to win with votes from the configuration-less restarted voters), then stops that configured voter and observes whether the two remaining live voters - a quorum of three, each holding every committed entry (log last index 13 on both) - can elect a leader within six seconds at 50ms timeouts.
assumptions: Restarting two voters while one keeps running is the ordinary rolling/cold restart an operator may perform; all three stores already contain the bootstrapped configuration entry and every committed entry.
The decision to stop the configured voter afterwards is a normal availability event (the node is gracefully shut down), not a fault injection: two of three voters remain alive and up to date.
A quorum of two live voters with complete logs is entitled to elect a leader in this cluster, which is exactly what the control case measures.
excluded: No partitions, no disk faults, no message loss, no injected delays.
The election fan-out to the stopped node is not traced; the observation is the absence of any leader among the live voters.

scope.description: Four in-process nodes at protocol version 3 with 300ms heartbeat/election/lease: A and B are bootstrapped as voters {A,B}; A snapshots, adds E as a caught-up nonvoter, adds C as a voter (config {A,B,C} plus nonvoter E), commits four commands. A is shut down and restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true so its in-memory configuration comes from the snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry; the other three nodes get longer timeouts so the restarted leader wins back leadership. B is then partitioned from A (C is already absent from A's stale configuration, so A replicates to nobody but E), and A issues one AddVoter E. Observations: whether that change commits and with whose acknowledgement, each side's configuration and log tail, who leads each side and in which term, and the content of A's log at the created entry index before and after the partition is healed.
assumptions: E is a caught-up nonvoter before the change, which is what lets the silently-created {A,B,E} configuration commit with A and E alone once B is partitioned; this is ordinary use of AddNonvoter followed by AddVoter.
Restarting the leader with RestoreCommittedLogs=true is the documented configuration already established by the earlier receipts; nothing else about the cluster changes.
The partition is applied by disconnecting the in-memory transports in both directions, which is a real partition for all Raft traffic (AppendEntries, heartbeats, votes).
Both sides keep following the protocol: A leads the {A,B,E} configuration with E's acknowledgements, and B and C campaign under their own {A,B,C} configuration after their election timeout.
excluded: No control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter adds a single server and the two-server change cannot arise; that is a source-level statement (nextConfiguration over the current configuration) rather than an execution.
No disk faults or message loss; the only partition is the one applied explicitly.

scope.description: Three-voter in-process cluster {A,B,C} at protocol version 3 with 50ms timeouts. A snapshots, then C is shut down for its own removal, RemoveServer C commits with {A,B}, two further commands push the persisted commit index past the removal entry, and A is restarted on the same stores with RestoreCommittedLogs (case restore_on) or without it (control restore_off). assumptions: C is offline for its own removal, so it never learns it was removed; that is an ordinary operator sequence (a failed node is removed while down and then comes back).
B and C both hold every entry up to the removal, so the entries, commit index and configurations come from real replication.
After the partition, {A,B} is the configuration committed in the log (removal entry committed), so an entry present only on A cannot be committed.

The probe does not assert what happens after the partition heals, which is the subject of the dual-majority harness.

interpretations.rationale: NewRaft documents that existing state such as logs and peers is restored (api.go 504-507) and RestoreCommittedLogs is documented only as replaying committed logs before startup (config.go 243-254); nothing waives configuration recovery. The code nevertheless bounds the configuration scan by max(lastSnapshot, lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613) while restoreFromCommittedLogs has already raised lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755). processConfigurationLogEntry is the only path that turns a log entry into r.configurations (raft.go 1605-1623), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are dropped whenever a snapshot does not carry them (snapshot path: api.go 645-689). Consequence: after a plain restart of a bootstrapped node with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, r.configurations.latest is empty, so runFollower refuses to campaign ('no known peers', raft.go 230-234) and both requestVote and requestPreVote skip their membership checks because they are gated on a non-empty Servers list (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784). The rule that decides the decision is therefore evaluated against an empty configuration rather than the replicated one.
counterevidence: The existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs (raft_test.go 1183-1280) passes: it always snapshots before restarting, so its configuration comes from snapshot metadata rather than from the log, and the same probe shows that a snapshot-carried configuration masks the loss.

The loss is not caused by the commit-tracking store or by replaying logs to the FSM per se: the control restart with RestoreCommittedLogs=false on identical stores and log contents keeps the configuration and wins the election again.
limitations: The executed probe is a single-voter in-memory cluster; the multi-node consequences (a node that grants votes to servers it cannot be shown to contain, or a node whose quorum size is computed from a stale configuration) are read from source, not executed.

The persisted commit index used at restart is what the store reported (6 while the log ended at 7); the drop of the configuration entry does not depend on that lag, but the exact boundary of what is skipped does.
Whether upstream intends applications to always snapshot before enabling this option is not stated anywhere in the captured sources; the Config documentation mentions no such requirement.

interpretations.rationale: Observed in the retained execution: after restart with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot, the node's configuration is empty (event index 1: mode=restore_on_no_snapshot, servers_before=1, servers_after=0, config_preserved=false, snapshot_count=0, staged_commit=6, log_last_index=7) and it never campaigns again (became_leader=false after a 3s opportunity, with the node logging 'no known peers, aborting election'), while the two controls keep the configuration and re-elect (index 3 restore_off_no_snapshot: servers_after=1, became_leader=true; index 5 restore_on_with_snapshot: servers_after=1, snapshot_count=1, became_leader=true). Source account of the mechanism: NewRaft documents that existing state such as logs and peers is restored (api.go 504-507) and RestoreCommittedLogs is documented only as replaying committed logs before startup (config.go 243-254); restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755) and the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never turned into r.configurations by their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). With Servers empty, runFollower refuses to start an election (raft.go 230-234) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).
counterevidence: The repository's own TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs (raft_test.go 1183-1280) passes because it always snapshots before restarting; the executed snapshot control (index 5) shows the same masking, so the failing case is specifically a configuration that lives only in the skipped committed log prefix.
Restarting identical durable state with RestoreCommittedLogs=false keeps servers_after=1 and re-elects (index 3), so neither the commit-tracking store nor replaying logs to the FSM is the cause.

The node still has all committed entries on disk (log_last_index=7 > commit_index=6), so this is a lost configuration context, not lost data; the entry itself is present and would be re-read only if a snapshot were installed.
limitations: Executed scope is a single-voter in-memory cluster (protocol version 3, heartbeat/election 50ms); the multi-node consequences (votes granted to servers the node cannot show it contains, quorum size and configuration changes computed from a stale base) are read from source and are the subject of the registered gap.
The restart uses the commit index the store reported (6, log end 7); the boundary of the skipped prefix depends on that value, but the omission of the configuration entry does not.
Nothing in the captured sources requires an application to snapshot before enabling RestoreCommittedLogs, so the failing condition is reachable through the documented configuration alone.

Observed at construction time (native run, pending retained receipt): with RestoreCommittedLogs=true the restarted node reports 2 servers while its peer still reports 3 and its own log's newest configuration entry (index 8) is below the persisted commit index (11); the next AddVoter then committed successfully (err=nil) with the cluster converging on 3 servers without C, so voter C was legitimately added and then silently removed without any request removing it. A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by retained receipt d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740: the restarted node adopts the snapshot-carried configuration when the newest configuration entry lies inside the replayed committed prefix (comparison 0 violated, witness index 1: servers_after=2 while the peer reports 3 and the newest configuration entry index 8 is below the staged commit index 11), and that stale base changes a real decision (comparison 2 violated, witness index 3: AddVoter E returned no error and both nodes ended with 3 members and contains_c_final=false, so voter C was silently removed). a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-gap-1.explanation: Partly answered by source and receipt trace, not yet executed. The obvious route cannot work: a voter that never receives the silently-created {A,B,E} entry is strictly behind in the log, and the log up-to-date check in requestVote/requestPreVote (raft.go 1731-1746, 1812-1828) makes any voter that holds the entry refuse to vote for it, so the removed voter C cannot win alone or with a lagging peer. A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

1ed9540f22fe4fa9bef3b3bda88e22e8-gap-2.explanation: Resolved by retained receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c (scored): the silent two-server change {A,B,C} -> {A,B,E} committed on A plus the promoted caught-up nonvoter E (parsed index 2: change_err nil, x_index 11, committed=true, entry type LogConfiguration on A and on E, A commit index 11, B still at log index 10); the old majority {B,C} elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, comparison violated with witness 3), i.e. two concurrent leaders with disjoint support over the same log; and after healing, A's entry at index 11 became a LogNoop of term 4 (parsed index 4, comparison violated with witness 4), so the entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs was truncated on the node that had committed it. The earlier receipt 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8 reproduced the same observations but its comparisons were unscored because of my identity wiring; it is retained as the superseded revision of the same harness.

counterevidence: The isolated control receipt edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d scores holds with the identical restart and no snapshot (servers_after=1), so the loss is caused by replaying the committed prefix, not by restart, snapshot absence, or the commit-tracking store.

The snapshot run inside the first receipt (index 5) keeps the configuration, so the defect requires the newest configuration entry to be inside the skipped prefix; a snapshot taken after the change masks it.
Voter C never runs in the two-voter probe, so nothing in the receipts shows C resisting or noticing its removal; the claim is about the configuration the running nodes decide with.

The cluster-wide receipt 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a scores the control comparison holds (index 3, nodes_with_full_config=3) and the failing case violated (index 1, nodes_with_full_config=0), so the empty configuration after a simultaneous restart is specific to the replayed committed prefix.

Receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837 scores the control comparison holds (index 3: the two live voters re-elect a leader without the flag) and the failing case violated (index 1: after the configured voter stops, no leader among the two live voters although both hold every committed entry, log last index 13 on both), so the loss of electability is tied to the missing configuration rather than to the restart or the shutdown.

The dual-majority path needs a caught-up nonvoter E so the silent change can commit without the partitioned voter B; without such a node the change would need B's acknowledgement and B would then hold the new membership.

Two independent executions of the corrected dual-majority experiment (receipts 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c and 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e) produced the same entry index, the same concurrent leadership and the same truncation, so the outcome is reproducible rather than a single-run timing artifact.
limitations: All executions are in-process in-memory clusters at protocol version 3 with 50ms heartbeat/election timeouts and a single committed configuration change; joint-consensus or multi-step changes are not exercised.

The multi-node progress consequence (a live quorum of up-to-date voters unable to elect after the configured voter stops) is the subject of the partial-restart experiment requested in this update; the authority consequence that configuration-less nodes still grant votes is observed indirectly there (the configured voter wins their votes) and read from source (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).
The finding is specific to RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag disabled the same durable state recovers normally in every receipt.

The configuration-less nodes still act as voters in other respects (they granted the configured voter's election win in receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837, index 0), which is why the cluster survived until that voter stopped; this is read from the receipt and from the membership checks being skipped for an empty configuration (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).

In that probe the partitioned side elects its leader with 3s election timeouts (reloaded to keep the restarted leader from losing the first election), so the interval is seconds; the ordering it demonstrates does not depend on those particular values.

The dual-majority probe has no control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter is a single-server change and cannot create disjoint majorities (nextConfiguration over the current configuration, configuration.go 224-302).

Leader concurrency on the two sides was observed in the two scored executions (A still leader in term 3 while B led term 4) but a later construction-time run of the extended harness observed A already stepped down when the old side's leader was sampled, so that window is schedule-dependent; the reproducible consequences are the truncation of the committed entry and the resulting FSM divergence.

The extended harness adds the client write and FSM observations; its retained receipt is requested in this update, so the FSM-divergence comparison is claimed from the construction-time run plus source (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, and lastApplied only moves forward, state.go 136-141) until that receipt exists.

A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

1ed9540f22fe4fa9bef3b3bda88e22e8-gap-2.explanation: Resolved by retained receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c (scored): the silent two-server change {A,B,C} -> {A,B,E} committed on A plus the promoted caught-up nonvoter E (parsed index 2: change_err nil, x_index 11, committed=true, entry type LogConfiguration on A and on E, A commit index 11, B still at log index 10); the old majority {B,C} elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, comparison violated with witness 3), i.e. two concurrent leaders with disjoint support over the same log; and after healing, A's entry at index 11 became a LogNoop of term 4 (parsed index 4, comparison violated with witness 4), so the entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs was truncated on the node that had committed it. The earlier receipt 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8 reproduced the same observations but its comparisons were unscored because of my identity wiring; it is retained as the superseded revision of the same harness.

counterevidence: The isolated control receipt edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d scores holds with the identical restart and no snapshot (servers_after=1), so the loss is caused by replaying the committed prefix, not by restart, snapshot absence, or the commit-tracking store.

The snapshot run inside the first receipt (index 5) keeps the configuration, so the defect requires the newest configuration entry to be inside the skipped prefix; a snapshot taken after the change masks it.
Voter C never runs in the two-voter probe, so nothing in the receipts shows C resisting or noticing its removal; the claim is about the configuration the running nodes decide with.

The cluster-wide receipt 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a scores the control comparison holds (index 3, nodes_with_full_config=3) and the failing case violated (index 1, nodes_with_full_config=0), so the empty configuration after a simultaneous restart is specific to the replayed committed prefix.

Receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837 scores the control comparison holds (index 3: the two live voters re-elect a leader without the flag) and the failing case violated (index 1: after the configured voter stops, no leader among the two live voters although both hold every committed entry, log last index 13 on both), so the loss of electability is tied to the missing configuration rather than to the restart or the shutdown.

The dual-majority path needs a caught-up nonvoter E so the silent change can commit without the partitioned voter B; without such a node the change would need B's acknowledgement and B would then hold the new membership.

Two independent executions of the corrected dual-majority experiment (receipts 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c and 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e) produced the same entry index, the same concurrent leadership and the same truncation, so the outcome is reproducible rather than a single-run timing artifact.

In that extended execution the stale leader had already stepped down when the old side's leader was sampled (index 4, a_still_leader=false), which is why leader concurrency is reported as an observed window from the two earlier executions rather than as a comparison in the current harness.
limitations: All executions are in-process in-memory clusters at protocol version 3 with 50ms heartbeat/election timeouts and a single committed configuration change; joint-consensus or multi-step changes are not exercised.

The multi-node progress consequence (a live quorum of up-to-date voters unable to elect after the configured voter stops) is the subject of the partial-restart experiment requested in this update; the authority consequence that configuration-less nodes still grant votes is observed indirectly there (the configured voter wins their votes) and read from source (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).
The finding is specific to RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag disabled the same durable state recovers normally in every receipt.

The configuration-less nodes still act as voters in other respects (they granted the configured voter's election win in receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837, index 0), which is why the cluster survived until that voter stopped; this is read from the receipt and from the membership checks being skipped for an empty configuration (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).

In that probe the partitioned side elects its leader with 3s election timeouts (reloaded to keep the restarted leader from losing the first election), so the interval is seconds; the ordering it demonstrates does not depend on those particular values.

The dual-majority probe has no control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter is a single-server change and cannot create disjoint majorities (nextConfiguration over the current configuration, configuration.go 224-302).

Leader concurrency on the two sides was observed in the two scored executions (A still leader in term 3 while B led term 4) but a later construction-time run of the extended harness observed A already stepped down when the old side's leader was sampled, so that window is schedule-dependent; the reproducible consequences are the truncation of the committed entry and the resulting FSM divergence.

The child question's retained receipt (ee57ec0448704270bcbc1cf7ace9a045) confirmed the resurrected membership but did not reach the premature-commit observation, because the stale leader lost the post-restart election to the correctly configured member in that execution; the child interpretation records this and requests the corrected harness.
interpretations.joint_history: All receipts belong to this question and were executed from the same snapshot. 430d7ba6 (empty configuration), d2d1cb09 (stale configuration and the silently dropped voter), edfd3c20 (isolated control, holds), 4f4a771f (all voters restart, cluster-wide progress loss), 7afe8c04 (live quorum cannot elect) and 79d93a5a (silent two-server change, concurrent leaders, truncation of the committed entry) form one chain: each was built from the previous receipt's outcome, and each uses the same bootstrap/commit/snapshot/restart operations rather than fabricated state.

interpretations.rationale: Retained receipt ee57ec0448704270bcbc1cf7ace9a045 establishes the membership half of this question: after a committed RemoveServer of the offline voter C and a restart with RestoreCommittedLogs, the restarted leader reports three servers including C and two peers while the continuously running member B reports two servers and one peer (comparison 0 violated, witness index 1). The write half was not reached in that execution: B won the election in term 3 immediately after A's restart (as the run log shows) and A was a follower when the write was issued, so the Apply returned a leadership error, the entry index in the observation was the pre-existing no-op and the quorum field was therefore vacuous; that comparison is recorded as not reached and is not used as evidence. The corrected harness (successor requested in this update) keeps the stale leader in power, records whether A leads before the partition and takes the compared index from the Apply future, so the premature-commit question can be decided by a retained receipt.
counterevidence: In the same receipt the control mode kept the committed membership (two servers) and the write prediction was not reached there either, so nothing in this receipt supports the premature-commit claim in either direction.
limitations: The premature-commit claim rests on a construction-time run of the corrected harness only; its retained receipt is requested in this update and until it exists the child defect judgment stays unresolved.

interpretations.rationale: Retained receipt b1daa1f4c9444b8d857bc7e0ab761691 scores all four comparisons as predicted. After a committed AddVoter D and a restart with RestoreCommittedLogs, the leader reports three servers and no longer contains D while the other three nodes report four (comparison 0 violated, witness index 1). With C and D disconnected, a single Apply on that leader succeeds: it commits and applies the entry at index 8 while C's log ends at 7 and D's at 6, so only two of the four committed voters hold it and the entry is not committed under the configuration in the log, which requires three (comparison 2 violated, witness index 3, voters_holding_entry=2, entry_on_committed_quorum=false). The controls hold: the same restart without the flag keeps four servers (index 5) and the same partition makes the write fail with 'leadership lost while committing log' (index 7). Mechanism: the in-memory configuration drives the quorum (configurationChangeChIfStable admits changes on stale indexes, appendConfigurationEntry derives membership from the stale base, commitment is installed from it on append), so a configuration missing a committed voter understates the quorum and lets the client be told a write succeeded.
counterevidence: The control mode on identical stores and the identical partition refuses the write, so the acceptance is attributable to the understated membership rather than to the partition.
limitations: The probe partitions C and D explicitly; a construction-time repeat is requested in this update because the outcome depends on the restarted leader winning its re-election and on the partition leaving A and B connected.

A repeat of the simultaneous-restart experiment reproduced the same failure and control values, so the headline progress claim also rests on two scored executions.

The same receipt's control mode kept 3 members and ended with 4 including C (observed at parsed index 5; that comparison was scored unknown because both modes shared a result event name, which the dedicated control experiment has now replaced with a scored holds).

a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-gap-1.explanation: Partly answered by source and receipt trace, not yet executed. The obvious route cannot work: a voter that never receives the silently-created {A,B,E} entry is strictly behind in the log, and the log up-to-date check in requestVote/requestPreVote (raft.go 1731-1746, 1812-1828) makes any voter that holds the entry refuse to vote for it, so the removed voter C cannot win alone or with a lagging peer. A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. (2) d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740 index 1: with a snapshot carrying {A,B}@1 and a committed AddVoter C at index 8 with staged commit 11, the restarted node reports 2 servers while its continuously running peer reports 3 and its own log still holds the newest configuration entry; index 3: a later AddVoter E then returns no error and both nodes converge on 3 members without C (contains_c_final=false), i.e. a legitimately added voter is silently removed from the cluster by a change computed from the stale base. (3) edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d index 1: the isolated control with RestoreCommittedLogs=false scores holds (servers_after=1 against the same bootstrapped voter), so the replayed committed prefix, not restart itself, is the cause. (4) 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a index 1: restarting all three voters at once with the flag leaves servers_after=[0,0,0] and nodes_with_full_config=0 with no leader in a six-second opportunity, while the same procedure without the flag scores holds at index 3 (nodes_with_full_config=3, leader elected) - a cluster-wide progress loss, not a single node's lost context. (5) 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837: with only two of three voters restarted, the untouched configured voter leads with the configuration-less nodes' votes (index 0, servers_after=[0,0,3]); once that voter stops, the two remaining live, fully up-to-date voters cannot elect a leader in six seconds at 50ms timeouts (index 1, log last index 13 on both), while the control without the flag re-elects immediately (index 3). Source chain: restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755); the configuration scan then begins at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never fed to their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). With Servers empty the follower refuses to campaign (raft.go 230-234 on every heartbeat timeout, raft.go 214-251) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784); with Servers stale, appendConfigurationEntry derives the next membership from that stale base (raft.go 1204-1241, configuration.go 224-302) once the admission gate sees latest==committed (raft.go 654-664). (6) 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8: with A's configuration coming from a snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry, AddVoter E returned no error and the silently created two-server change committed at index 11 with A's commit index at 11 and E holding the same LogConfiguration entry (parsed index 2), while B stayed at log index 10 with the old membership; the old majority {B,C} then elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, a_still_leader=true), and after the partition healed A's entry 11 was a LogNoop of term 4 rather than the committed configuration entry (parsed index 4, committed_entry_truncated=true). Receipt e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064 (extended harness) scores both comparisons violated with witness index 5: the entry at the created index is truncated after healing, and after a client command returned success and was acknowledged and committed on the {A,B,E} leader (parsed index 3: write_applied=true, applied_a=12, fsm_a_logs=6) the FSM contents differ afterwards (fsm_a_logs=6 versus fsm_b_logs=5), so the client-visible effect survives only on the node whose log lost the entry. Summary of the current account for this question: the trigger is RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, a log whose newest configuration entry is at or below the persisted commit index, and no snapshot whose ConfigurationIndex covers that entry. Under that trigger the restarted node reconstructs its configuration only from the snapshot, so three consequence classes follow, each with retained control-backed receipts: (a) a missing membership context - empty configuration when there is no snapshot, which stops all campaigns and leaves a live quorum unable to elect (receipts 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc, 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a, 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837); (b) decisions taken from a stale base - a single AddVoter becomes the two-server change {A,B,C}->{A,B,E}, which silently drops a voter, and with a partitioned old voter produces concurrent leaders over the same log, truncation of the entry the stale leader had committed and divergent FSM state (receipts d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740, 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c, 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e and e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064); (c) stale membership accounting - a resurrected removed voter or a forgotten added voter makes the leader accept writes that the configuration committed in the log has not acknowledged (receipts 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 with 7adf927d528b4a74942c03b155aa8557, and b1daa1f4c9444b8d857bc7e0ab761691 with ec2c61af79bd42d7a5fe00657b7aeb22). In the empty-configuration cases the first two repairs need a leader, which is exactly what the empty configuration prevents. A repeat of the simultaneous-restart experiment reproduced the same failure and control values, so the headline progress claim also rests on two scored executions.
